subject: physics_2
question_text: What is the ratio of speed of infrared rays and ultraviolet rays in vacuum?

mark_split.label: Both travel at the speed of light

verification.note: The 1+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. For this Paper-II bank the two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only, and the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers. Hand-checked: every electromagnetic wave travels through vacuum at c = 3 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹ regardless of wavelength, so infrared and ultraviolet have the same vacuum speed and the ratio is 1 : 1, as the book answers (p.41).

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Both travel at the speed of light
steps.mark_note: Both move at c = 3 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹
lines: In vacuum, infrared rays and ultraviolet
rays both travel at the speed of light,
steps.margin_note: First mark. The reason: speed in vacuum does not depend on wavelength.
steps.why: Every electromagnetic wave, whatever its wavelength, moves through vacuum at the same speed c. The speed changes only inside a material medium.
common_mistakes: Giving ultraviolet a higher speed because it has a higher frequency. In vacuum, frequency changes nothing about the speed.
Quoting c without units. Write 3 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹.

recall.must_convey: That infrared and ultraviolet rays both travel at the speed of light in vacuum.
accept: both travel at three into ten power eight
both travel at the speed of light

steps.memory_tip: In vacuum every part of the electromagnetic spectrum shares one speed, c.

steps.label: The ratio 1 : 1
lines: So the ratio of their speeds is 1 : 1.
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Write the ratio itself, not only that the speeds are equal.
steps.why: The question asks for a ratio, so the answer line must show 1 : 1. Equal speeds is the reason; 1 : 1 is the asked answer.
common_mistakes: Stopping at both have the same speed and never writing 1 : 1. The asked quantity is the ratio.
Writing a ratio of wavelengths or frequencies. Those differ between infrared and ultraviolet; only the vacuum speeds are equal.

recall.must_convey: That the ratio of the speeds is one to one.

steps.memory_tip: Same speed, so the ratio can only be 1 : 1.

insider_note: The trap is inventing a difference — the examiner wants 1 : 1 with the reason that vacuum speed does not depend on wavelength.
